answers.answer: Keep 4 tokens of each of the five gem colors and all 5 gold tokens; reveal 3 nobles. Remove the other 7 nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 players: 4 gems per color, 5 gold, 3 nobles; Setup: 'Remove remaining noble tiles from the game'.

answers.answer: Three players use 5 tokens per gem color, 5 gold tokens and 4 nobles. Four players use 7 per gem color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more of each gem color and one more noble, with gold unchanged.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count table: 3 = 5/5/4; 4 = 7/5/5.

answers.answer: Shuffle each level separately. Arrange decks in a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 on top. Reveal 4 cards per level, 12 total in a 3×4 grid. The youngest player starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player: 'The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise.'

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different colors; take 2 non-gold gems of one color only if at least 4 are present before taking; reserve 1 face-up card or top card of a level deck only while holding fewer than 3 reserved cards, gaining 1 gold if available; or buy 1 face-up market card or 1 card reserved on an earlier turn by paying its cost after bonuses, using gold as a substitute if desired. You cannot take gems and buy in the same turn, or reserve and buy that card in the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of the four listed actions; purchase is of '1 card you reserved on a previous turn'.

answers.answer: All tokens you own, including gold, must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.'

answers.answer: You may take 2 green from 4, leaving 2. You cannot take 2 red from 3. The threshold is checked before taking, requiring at least 4 of that color. Neither gem-taking action permits gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure action 2: 'at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them'; both gem-taking actions specify no gold.

answers.answer: Temporarily holding 12 is allowed. Return 2 tokens of your choice to reach 10 by the end of the turn; these can include either or both newly drawn gems. Gold counts toward the 10-token limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'may temporarily exceed 10'; 'return tokens of their choice'; 'including gold'; 'some or all of the tokens they just took'.

answers.answer: Reserve the card and take 1 gold, temporarily reaching 11 tokens; return any 1 token, including that gold if desired, to end at 10. If gold is empty, you may still reserve, receive no gold and stay at 10 tokens.
answers.evidence: Reserve: 'If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold'; Hand Limit permits returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve either 1 face-up market card or the top card of any of the three level decks. A deck-top reservation is taken without showing it to opponents. Only its reserving player may buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: face-up card or 'top card'; 'without revealing it to other players'; 'only ... the player who reserved them'.

answers.answer: You cannot reserve a fourth card or reserve just to obtain gold while already holding 3 reservations. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; its only exit from your hand is to purchase it.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: 'If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another'; 'only way to remove ... is to purchase it'.

answers.answer: Immediately replace the reserved face-up level-2 card with the top card of the level-2 deck. Buying a face-up card causes the same immediate replacement from its level. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy and needs no replacement. If a market vacancy's level deck is empty, that space remains empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: 'Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved ... immediately replaced'; 'If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty'.

answers.answer: The 2 blue bonuses cover both blue costs, leaving 1 green token to spend (or 1 gold substitute). If bonuses cover every color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give this exact 2-blue/1-green example; bonuses act as a 'permanent gem' and may enable purchase 'without spending any tokens at all'.

answers.answer: Yes. The bonuses reduce the remaining cost to 1 blue, 1 black and 1 white. Spend the blue token for blue and 1 gold each for black and white. All 3 spent tokens return to the supply. Your bonus cards remain with you and keep their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce required tokens; gold 'can substitute for any single gem token'; spent gems and gold return to supply; bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Buy 1 face-up development from the market or 1 card you reserved on a previous turn, paying its cost after bonuses with permitted tokens or gold. Put purchased cards face-up before you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so their bonuses and prestige values remain visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card; Turn Structure action 4; 'sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible ... at all times'.

answers.answer: No: you have only 2 white bonuses, and a white or gold token cannot supply the third. A third white bonus would qualify you at the end of that turn, assuming the noble remains available; you receive at most 1 noble per turn. Exceeding any requirement is allowed.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: requires 'at least' the shown bonuses; 'bonuses only ... not gem tokens'; 'at most one noble per turn'.

answers.answer: Choose exactly 1 of the 2 nobles; you cannot take both or decline all. The automatic visit uses no additional action, gives 3 prestige points and is checked at the end of your turn after your action and token-limit check. The other noble remains available.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: 'cannot refuse'; 'not an action'; 'choose one'; '3 prestige points'; Turn Structure orders token-limit check before noble visit.

answers.answer: Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.'

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns; A takes no extra turn. The game then ends with equal turn counts. B is not guaranteed to win: another player may finish with more prestige, or win a tie with fewer purchased development cards.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round so everyone has the same turns; End-of-Game Clarifications: trigger player 'may not necessarily win'; Tiebreaker: fewest purchased developments.

answers.answer: You reach 16 prestige (13 + 3). This triggers the end condition because it is 15 or more, including noble points. Complete the current round to equalize turns, then determine the winner by most prestige and, if tied, fewest purchased developments.
answers.evidence: Nobles: 3 points; End-Game Trigger: '15 or more'; Determining the Winner and Tiebreaker.

answers.answer: B wins. A and B tie at 16 prestige, and B's 9 purchased developments beat A's 10. C's 15 points cannot win despite having fewer developments. Nobles count toward prestige. B's 3 unpurchased reserved cards do not count as purchased developments.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: purchased cards and nobles; Tiebreaker: 'fewest development cards purchased'; reserved cards remain unpurchased until bought.

answers.answer: None of those 8 printed points count toward scoring or the 15-point trigger, and neither white bonus reduces costs or qualifies for nobles until its reserved card is bought.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: points printed on each 'purchased card'; Payment: bonuses from 'previously purchased' cards; Noble Visits: bonuses 'from purchased development cards'.

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased zero-point card gives a permanent blue discount for future purchases and its bonus can qualify you for a noble despite its zero prestige value.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: each purchased card adds one permanent bonus; 'never generate tokens'; cards may have 0 prestige; nobles require purchased-card bonuses.

answers.answer: No: the card's own future bonus cannot pay its purchase cost, so with no existing blue bonus, blue token or gold you cannot buy it. In the separate white-card example, the newly purchased white bonus counts when checking for a noble at the end of this same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment uses bonuses from 'previously purchased development cards'; Noble Visits checks at end of turn using purchased cards.

answers.answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot cover green or generate blue tokens as change. The blue cost is fully covered; you still owe 2 green, paid with 2 green tokens, 2 gold, or 1 of each.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: 'excess provides no benefit ... (no "change" is given)'; bonuses are discounts of their color; gold substitutes for any single gem.

answers.answer: The first noble does not use up the permanent bonuses. If the second noble remains available, taking gems on your next turn can still end with receiving it because you still qualify. You cannot collect it during an opponent's intervening turn; visits occur at the end of your own turn, at most 1 per turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent; Noble Visits: 'At the end of their turn'; multiple qualifying nobles: others 'remain available for future turns'.

answers.answer: Yes. With 0 reserved cards you may reserve the face-up level-3 card even if unaffordable, without paying its purchase cost. Take 1 gold if available. Reservation takes exactly 1 card and requires fewer than 3 reserved cards.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card permits a face-up card without a payment requirement, and grants 1 gold if available; purchase payment is a separate action.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled, so all 12 face-up cards remain. You take exactly 1 top card into your reserved hand, with no second replacement card in hand; take 1 gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve permits taking 'top card' from a deck; Card Replacement applies to face-up cards removed from the grid; Turn Structure: 'Reserve 1 development card'.

answers.answer: The four face-up cards remain available to buy or reserve under the usual conditions. Buying one leaves its space empty permanently because that deck cannot refill it; the other 3 remain available.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: 'unless that level's deck is exhausted'; 'empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game'; deck exhaustion does not end game.

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may choose to buy the 1 affordable reserved card or take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different available color piles. Those are alternative single actions, and the normal prestige end condition still applies.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'Exhausting the development decks or the face-up market does not end the game'; 'remaining legal actions, including purchasing reserved cards'.

answers.answer: Yes. Take 1 token from each of the 3 different available non-gold gem colors, temporarily hold 13, and return all 3 newly drawn tokens to end with the original 10. No net token gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: temporary excess permitted; 'may return some or all of the tokens they just took'.

answers.answer: A returns both spent gold to the supply, making 2 available. B then reserves 1 card and takes 1 of those gold, leaving 1 in the supply before any token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment: 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'; Reserve: 'take 1 gold token ... from the supply'.

answers.answer: Yes. You may buy the affordable face-up level-3 card immediately; the listed purchase action has no lower-level purchase or unlocking requirement.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card'.

answers.answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble visit. You finish with 18 prestige (12 + 3 from the card + 3 from the noble). Players who still have a turn in the current round continue until everyone has had the same number of turns.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: automatic and cannot be refused; noble value 3; End-Game Trigger: complete current round after reaching 15 or more.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes this turn, including end-of-turn checks. A starts no new round and nobody gets an extra turn: A, B, C and D have now taken the same number of turns.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns'.

answers.answer: Do not reveal a replacement: the 7 removed nobles remain out of the game permanently. The acquired tile goes face-up in the recipient's play area, leaving 2 nobles available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: 'Noble tiles removed during setup are out of the game permanently'; Noble Visits: received tile face-up in front of you.

answers.answer: Emerald is green, diamond white, sapphire blue, onyx black, ruby red and gold joker yellow. There are 90 development cards: 40 level 1, 30 level 2 and 20 level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token-color table; Development Cards table: 40/30/20, 90 total.

answers.answer: You may spend the 1 gold instead of the green and keep the green; no requirement to spend the matching gem first is stated. Return the spent gold to the supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token'; 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'.

answers.answer: Yes. Take 1 red, 1 blue and 1 green, leaving 0 red, 1 blue and 2 green. The four-token threshold applies only to taking 2 tokens of the same color, not to the three-different-colors action.
answers.evidence: Take 3: 'Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles'; Take 2 requires at least 4 of its color.

answers.answer: A direct gold-for-red exchange is not one of the four permitted actions, and the joker rule does not authorize that exchange. When purchasing a development, each gold may substitute for any 1 required gem token and is then returned to the supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of four actions; Payment: gold 'can substitute for any single gem token'.

answers.answer: You must choose exactly 1 of the four legal actions; voluntary passing is not allowed when legal actions are available.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'a player must perform exactly one of the following four actions'.

answers.answer: Sort the gem and gold tokens by color into 6 distinct piles, placed within reach of all players.
answers.evidence: Setup step 5: '6 distinct piles sorted by color, within reach of all players'.

answers.answer: Your final prestige is 15: 12 from purchased developments plus 3 from the acquired noble. The 4 unspent gold and 5 other gem tokens add no prestige points.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources lists purchased development values and noble tiles at 3 each; tokens are not a prestige-point source.
